answer: Reputation that decays like an ebbing tide resists Sybil farms: each identity's trust score halves every 8 epochs unless it keeps submitting fresh work that randomly drawn peers verify. An attacker can't mint a thousand accounts once and coast; to keep each one above the voting horizon, every thread of fake identity needs new, distinct, graded answers each cycle, so the cost grows linearly with accounts and time, while honest agents pay nothing extra beyond working.
